MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 10, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on May 10, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on May 5, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:06 pm)
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs Sachs

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation(Paragraph (1) of Subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9) Name of Case: (Michael Schlesinger v. City of Mission Viejo)

CS2. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Liberty Mutual and
  Yasin: Agency Claimed Against - City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) Section 54956.9 (2 cases)

City Council Minutes  1  May 10, 2022
 CS3. Conference with Labor Negotiators (Government Code Section 54957.6) Agency
  Designated Representatives: Dennis Wilberg, Cheryl Dyas, and Monique Goetz.
  Unrepresented Employees: Animal Services Department Personnel.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four City Council Members present and Mayor Pro Tem
Sachs absent.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced there were three properly agenized Closed Session Items. The
City Council was updated as to facts and circumstances. No actions were taken therefore no
reportable actions were taken.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked that Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley run for re-election for a
two-year term in 2022 instead of extending their terms to 2024. She pointed out the resolutions
from 2020 stated two seats for two years. She quoted the City Attorney on his statement from the
March 22 Minutes and scolded the City Attorney for misleading the voters.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Questioned Mayor Pro Tem Sachs’ comments from the March 22 Minutes
regarding the golf course and asked where the fourteen million dollars to pay off the golf course
came from.

Nancy Van Deusen, M.V.: Commented on the condition of the Garden Plaza and asked if heritage
is a throwaway. She asked the City Council to keep the current zoning as office professional.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Questioned the Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley on extending their
terms an additional two years and asked by what evidence permits them to serve an additional two
years without a vote of the residents. He further challenged Mayor Bucknum, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
and Council Member Raths to answer the same questions. He also stated that Attorney Curley has
never answered his questions pertaining to this. Urged that Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley
run for election in 2022.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: He shared that for the future the City needs to stay true to the community
and future challenges from opportunists and stay true to the founders of this great planned city. He
suggested that we adopt more well-defined protections in the City Council’s control to protect
citizens of Mission Viejo for opportunists like ValueRock Realty.

City Council Minutes  2  May 10, 2022
 Nonny Bailey, M.V.: Asked that Council Member’s uphold the Planning Commission’s decision
to deny the re-zoning of the Garden Plaza. She voiced concerns over vehicle noise at the
intersection of La Paz and Marguerite during the night. Quoted from the California Vehicle Code
and the City code regarding noise element reports. Asked if signs could be installed to enforce the
vehicle noise violations along with speed limits.

Ken Kisling, M.V.: Commented on the results of the City Survey that was discussed at the last
meeting. He suggested the City try harder to encourage residences to sign up for the e-newsletter
to stay informed. Questioned why the question of mixed-use housing was on the survey and asked
the Council to state whether they are for or against it.

Maggie Fleitman, San Clemente: Raised concerns to the City Council regarding the fentanyl
poisoning of our children. Spoke about her support group called “Solace for Hope” that meets
every month at the Norman P. Community Center the second and fourth Wednesday monthly.
Lastly, she asked what the City is doing about this crisis and offered her assistance in educating the
community.

Yin Lu, M.V.: Voiced her frustration with lack of notification to residents on the proposed projects
such as ValueRock project, the 5-G Tower in her neighborhood, and the General Plan Element that
was adopted by the City Council last October. She highlighted some of the General Plan Element
and encouraged residents to get a copy and review it. Suggested that the City Council and the
Planning Department send out notices directly to the residents regarding proposed plans and zone
changes.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Sachs

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 26, 2022, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated April 15, 2022 in the Amount of $2,634,540.92

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated April 22, 2022 in the Amount of $1,146,784.71

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  May 10, 2022
 4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2022

  Received and filed.

5.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for March 2022

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2022

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2022

  Received and filed.

8.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter Ending March 31, 2022

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter Ending
  March 31, 2022.

9.  Community Services Grant Funding Program Allocations

  Approved the Community Services Commission's grant funding recommendations for 2022.

10. Amendment to Agreement with JHD Planning, LLC to Update the General Plan
  Housing Element (6th Cycle)

  Approved Second Amendment with JHD Planning, LLC for an additional $50,620, resulting
  in a not-to-exceed amount of $133,532 to update the General Plan Housing Element, and
  extending the term of the Agreement through June 30, 2023.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

11. Development Code Amendment DCA21-20- being a separate application and petition
  submitted by Patrick Cox for, and as agent of, ValueRock Realty, on October 6, 2021,
  to amend the City of Mission Viejo Development Code and establish a new Mixed-Use
  Zoning District, including a mix of permissible new land uses and development
  standards. DCA2021-20 is considered in advance of ValueRock Realty’s development
  application, which includes General Plan Amendment GPA2021-36, Zone Change
  ZC2021-24, Planned Development Permit PDP2021-321, Variance VAR2021-58 and
  Tentative Tract Map TTM19159, for the development of a mixed-use project. The yet
  incomplete future project is referenced as "The Gardens" and is on a 6.5-acre site
  located at 27001 La Paz Road, currently zoned OP (Office/Professional). The
City Council Minutes  4  May 10, 2022
   anticipated "The Gardens" project is reported to include ground floor retail uses
  totaling 48,000 sq. ft., four upper stories of residential development totaling 234
  apartment units, and both surface and structured parking for a total of 626 parking
  spaces

  Mayor Bucknum opened the Public Hearing at 6:43 p.m.

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Richard Schweinberg, M.V.: Made suggestions for other mixed-use locations and asked that
  the Council deny this application.

  Adriana Brady, M.V.: Raised concerns that ValueRock is not going to give up and asked
  about the Chick fil A replacing The Claim Jumper with lack of communication to residents
  about various projects within the City. She also raised concerns about the fentanyl crisis
  coming across the border.

  Bryan Zuetel, M.V.: Voiced that he supports staff recommendation to deny the re-zone of the
  Garden Plaza. Commented that mix-use will be coming to the City as we have to satisfy
  Sacramento, but stated that the corner of Marguerite and La Paz is not the location.

  Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Stated that he started the “Stop the Monster” campaign and that they
  will be the guardians of the City if need be. Outlined the efforts that his group made during
  this campaign. Outlined ValueRock and pointed out the reasons this company is not a
  developer but opportunists.

  Natalie Parsons, M.V.: Stated how much she loves Mission Viejo and asked that the Council
  not re-zone the Garden Plaza.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that City Attorney Curley crafted a process for a desired outcome
  and quoted city resolution stating that Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley were elected
  for a term of two years. Read an excerpt from a letter by Value Rock’s attorneys. Lastly, she
  read off the Council Members 497 (24-hour/10-day Contribution Report) filings from past
  elections.

  Christopher Lance, M.V.: Addressed the Council that he has been a resident for the past nine
  years and voiced concern over the increase of traffic in the City. Pointed out various
  environmental impacts of mixed-use developments.

  Bob Knoke, M.V.: Raised concerns regarding traffic and asked that the Council listen to the
  Planning Commission and Traffic Committee and deny the re-zone of the Garden Plaza.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg encouraged everyone that signed the petition opposing this
  project to send a letter to Sacramento opposing Assembly Bill 2011. The City has taken a
  position against it. He quoted from AB2011 “Notwithstanding any inconsistent provision of
  a local government’s general plan, specific plan, zoning ordinance, or regulation, a housing
  development shall be a use by right within a zone where office, retail, or parking are a
City Council Minutes  5  May 10, 2022
   principally permitted use.” He stated that if this Bill passes the City will have no say in
  ValueRock coming right back in and putting their project on the sight we are talking about.

  The Council Members gave their input.

  Mayor Bucknum closed the Public Hearing at 7:52 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt
  Resolution 22-09 Denying Development Code Amendment DCA21-20.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

13. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Fire Chief Capobianco.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Wilberg introduced the new Chief of Police Services Chris McDonald.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Curley introduced the new Planning Manager Jennifer Lowe.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell spoke about his trip to Europe and the cities he visited had many
mixed-use housing developments. He stated he is glad to be back.

City Council Minutes  6  May 10, 2022
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley attended the Mission Viejo Girls Softball closing ceremonies on April
29. On May 1 she attended the Water Safety event at the Marguerite Aquatics Center. She stated
she attended the Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for Raising Cane’s on Crown Valley Parkway.
Council Member Kelley announced there is a blood shortage and the City will be hosting a blood
drive on June 21 and you can make an appointment through redcross.org website.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths welcomed our new Police Chief Chris McDonald and Planning Manager
Jennifer Lowe. Stated he has been on the Council for eight years and stated that the Stop the Monster
is the largest public interest he has seen. He stated that he attended both Amazon Fresh and Raising
Cane’s grand opening. He also attended the Annual Day of Prayer. Council Member Sachs attended
Santa Margarita Water Fest this past Saturday. Lastly, he said it’s been a great two weeks and
thanked those that participated this evening and reminded residents about the Primary Election on
June 8.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum thanked Maggie Fleitman on her support group “Solace for Hope”. She indicated
that the City is working with County Supervisor Don Wagner and Senator Pat Bates on the fentanyl
crisis. Council Member Bucknum announced that this Thursday at 6:00 pm she will be hosting a
Sober Living Town Hall in the Council Chamber. She asked staff to give an update on the Chick
fil A going in where the current Claim Jumper restaurant is now. Attorney Curley announced that
the Planning Commission approved the application at last night’s meeting. Mayor Bucknum shared
that she was appointed Chair to the Orange County Council of Governments. She stated that this
the entity that feeds into the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) which will
give her a lot of impact on housing and policy. She encouraged residents to visit the pop-up Paseo
across the street. Assistant City Manager Rattay gave an outline of the pop-up and some of the
events that will be coming up. Lastly, she announced that this Saturday there will be an E-Waste
and Hazardous Household Disposal event in the parking lot at City Hall

ADJOURNMENT AT 8:19 P.M. TO TUESDAY, MAY 24, 2022, AT 5:00 P.M.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 24, 2022

City Council Minutes  7  May 10, 2022
